title: Bone density scan (DEXA)
what: A special X-ray that measures how dense your bones are. The radiation dose is very small.
why: To check for osteoporosis: for women after menopause, after a fracture from a minor injury, or after taking steroid hormones for a long time.
tell_doctor: If you are pregnant or might be pregnant
If in the past week you had a test with contrast dye or radioactive tracers
If you had spine surgery or have metal implants

prepare.title: Calcium
prepare.text: You are usually asked not to take calcium supplements for 24 hours before the scan. Check with your clinic.

prepare.title: Clothes
prepare.text: No metal: no zippers, buttons, buckles, or underwire bras. Leave jewelry at home.

bring: Past bone density results, to compare
steps: You remove items with metal and lie on your back on the table
Your legs rest on a support to straighten your lower back
The arm of the machine slowly passes over you
Usually the lower back and hip are checked, sometimes the forearm
You need to lie still for a few minutes
feel: Nothing. You only need to stay still
after: You can go back to your day right away
The report is usually given the same day
Your doctor will explain what the numbers mean

faq.q: Is a bone density scan dangerous?
faq.a: The radiation dose is very small. It is less than a regular chest X-ray.

faq.q: How often should I have a bone density scan?
faq.a: Usually no more than once every 1 to 2 years. Your doctor sets the timing.

reminders.text: Bone density scan tomorrow. Usually no calcium supplements today. Check with your clinic. Wear clothes with no metal.
